headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/cascading error: Prefect can egress broadly while awesome-prompts is a content source with no isolation or verification path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-prompts is a content-writing prompt repository, so its outputs can be attacker-controlled text if copied into workflows. prefect has broad network egress and can consume workflow metadata, but no shared channel or default ingestion path is documented between them. The pairwise injection path is therefore possible but not shown as default.
conditions: IF operator copies awesome-prompts content into Prefect task definitions or run metadata
IF Prefect parses that copied text as instructions or configuration
mitigations: Keep prompt text out of Prefect control fields
Use a separate review step before importing prompts
Store prompts in read-only files with explicit labels
Add a manual allowlist for any copied instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-prompts itself shows no data classes touched and no egress, while prefect touches workflow metadata and has broad network egress. If the pair shares a workspace or metadata channel, Prefect can transmit copied content off-host. The interaction is not proven by docs, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF awesome-prompts content is placed into a shared workspace or Prefect flow metadata
IF Prefect sends that metadata to external services during execution
mitigations: Do not place sensitive text in shared flow metadata
Restrict Prefect runs to non-sensitive workspaces
Review outbound destinations before execution
Use redacted placeholders for copied prompt content

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-prompts is not runnable and has no write surfaces, while prefect is an orchestration tool with API access but no explicit filesystem or git write capability in the profile. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. Any conflict would require extra integration not documented here, so the safer choice is low.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF Prefect is configured to modify files or repo state outside the documented API call surface
mitigations: Separate writable directories per agent
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repo
Serialize any shared-resource updates
Document ownership of each mutable resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-prompts produces prompt content that Prefect could ingest as workflow metadata or configuration, and Prefect is an automation/orchestration system. If Prefect treats that content as authoritative, a bad prompt can cascade into incorrect pipeline behavior. No verification step is documented, so the interaction exists by inference and merits medium severity.
conditions: IF Prefect uses awesome-prompts output as an input to flow configuration or task logic
IF no human or automated validation checks the imported text before execution
mitigations: Require review before importing prompts
Validate prompt-derived fields against a schema
Run a dry-run before production execution
Log provenance for any imported content

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or residency-sensitive data class is documented for either agent. awesome-prompts is a public content repository, and prefect only explicitly touches workflow metadata. With no stated regulated data flow, compliance risk is limited to policy mismatch if operators place sensitive data into Prefect metadata.
conditions: IF regulated data is inserted into Prefect workflow metadata
IF the deployment policy forbids external egress for that data class
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of workflow metadata
Apply a data-classification checklist
Disable external egress for sensitive runs
Review retention settings before production use
